cards.text: Psalm 33 doesn't name its writer, and it opens LOUD with a call to the righteous: "Rejoice in the LORD, O righteous ones…" Friend, rejoicing is the one thing I never need a recipe for.

cards.question: The writer calls the righteous ones to rejoice in the LORD. True or false: He says it is fitting for the upright to praise Him.

cards.text: Then the writer starts handing out the music: the harp, ten strings, and a new song to sing to the LORD. Friend, I play ZERO strings, so in this band I'm the guy in the back just clapping along.

cards.question: The writer calls for the harp, ten strings and a new song for the LORD. True or false: He wants this new song played quietly with no shouting.

cards.text: Why all the shouting? Because the word of the LORD is upright, and friend, when I tell you a batch will be ready in five minutes, that's not upright, that's a WISH.

cards.question: The word of the LORD is upright. True or false: The writer says some of the LORD's work can't be trusted.

cards.text: Then the writer tells us what the LORD loves: righteousness and justice. Not likes, baker, LOVES.

cards.question: The LORD loves righteousness and justice. Looking at the whole earth, what does the writer say it's full of?

cards.text: Then the writer goes way back: by the word of the LORD the heavens were made. Not built. SPOKEN.

cards.question: The heavens were made by the word of the LORD. What does the writer say all the stars were made by?

cards.text: The LORD piles up the waters of the sea and puts the depths into storehouses. The SEA, friend. Piled. Stored. Put away.

cards.question: After the seas and the stars, the writer calls for a response. True or false: He says only the people of Israel should fear the LORD.

cards.text: Why? The writer says, "For He spoke, and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm." Then he turns to the nations and the plans they make.

cards.question: The writer turns to the plans of the nations. What does he say the LORD does with them?
The nations' plans get frustrated. But the writer says the counsel of the LORD stands ___.

cards.text: And the purposes of His heart go on to all generations.
The nations' plans get frustrated. But now the writer names a nation that IS blessed.

cards.question: Which nation does the writer call blessed?

answers.text: The nation whose God is the LORD
The nation with the largest army
The nation with the richest king

cards.text: They're the people He has chosen as His inheritance! Friend, I got picked out of a bakery's closing-sale bin for 25 cents, so believe me, being chosen is a BIG deal.

cards.question: The LORD looks down from heaven. Who does the writer say He sees?

cards.text: From His dwelling place He gazes on all who live on the earth. And He shapes the hearts of each one.

cards.question: The LORD shapes the hearts of each person. True or false: The writer says He pays no attention to what they do.
Next the writer looks at a king with a vast army. True or false: He says the king is saved by that army.

cards.text: And no warrior is delivered by his great strength either. Then the writer points at the horse, with all its great strength.

cards.question: When it comes to being saved, what does the writer call a horse?

cards.text: Even its great strength cannot save. Friend, this mustache can lift a FULL cookie box, and it never once lifted me out of that junk drawer.

cards.question: Armies, strength and horses can't save. But the eyes of the LORD are on those who ___ Him and whose ___ is in His loving devotion.
The LORD keeps His eyes on those who hope in His loving devotion. What for?

answers.text: To test their faith in Him

cards.text: And He keeps them alive in famine, when food runs short. Not just in the good seasons, friend, but in the lean ones too.
Now the psalm gets personal: "Our soul waits for the LORD…" Friend, waiting is my WORST skill in the bakery, because I stand at the oven window like staring makes it bake faster.

cards.question: While their soul waits for the LORD, what does the writer call Him?
True or false: The writer says their hearts rejoice in the LORD because they trust in His holy name.

cards.text: And the psalm ends with a prayer straight to the LORD: "May Your loving devotion rest on us, O LORD, as we put our hope in You." It started with harps and shouting, and it lands right here, hoping in Him.
